title: Navigation Engine Task Response
description: Structured result returned by the generic navigation engine after a run completes (successfully, blocked, failed, or limit-exhausted). Raw website-derived evidence (captures) is kept separate from engine-generated classifications/reasoning (engineAssessment), per design requirement #8.

schemaVersion.description: Version of this task-response contract, e.g. "1.12.0". Bumped from "1.11.0" to "1.12.0" for the generic cross-client analytics-capture-evidence fix (see CLAUDE.md and docs/architecture.md "Generic action-attributed analytics capture"): captures.data_layer_evidence[] and captures.ga4_network_events[] entries now carry capture-context provenance (source: "main_frame"/"child_frame"/"popup_context", contextId, frameOrigin, truncated); ga4_network_events[] also gained method, postDataRaw, postDataParams, measurementId, and consentState so POST/sendBeacon GA4 requests are no longer only partially captured; captures.cta_clicks[] gained openedNewContext/observedNewContext reporting whether a click opened a popup/new-tab context and whether that context was actually instrumented before being closed, rather than closed unobserved. All new fields are additive and optional -- no existing field was removed, renamed, or had its meaning changed. Version of this task-response contract, e.g. "1.11.0". Bumped from "1.10.0" to "1.11.0" for the overlay-click-detection fix (see CLAUDE.md and docs/architecture.md "Modal-aware observation" / "Overlay-click side effect detection"): observation.activeDialog (see $defs/observation) reports a compact, generic identity (role + short accessible-name excerpt) for a visible dialog/modal surface (role="dialog", aria-modal="true", or a native <dialog>), when one is present in the main document; observation.interactiveElements[].nearestHeadingText surfaces the nearest enclosing heading's text, found via a bounded ancestor walk, so repeated-card/list-item controls that share an identical role+accessibleName (e.g. the same-labelled action button under several different listing cards) can be told apart for route-memory candidate identity; actionResult.clickSideEffectDetected and actionResult.fallbackVerified report, respectively, whether a click that looked intercepted/timed-out was instead recognised as having actually succeeded from generic post-click evidence, and whether a generic destinationUrl navigation fallback's resulting page state was verified as a meaningful change rather than assumed equivalent to a real click. All four fields are additive and optional -- no existing field was removed, renamed, or had its meaning changed. Bumped from "1.9.0" to "1.10.0" earlier because diagnostics.milestoneEvidence (see $defs/milestoneEvidenceRecord) was added: one record per success criterion, appended the moment it first becomes satisfied, explaining which page it was evaluated against, which phase of the step, and what evidence (a matched URL pattern, a matched selector, a deterministic vocabulary-overlap score, or a semanticVerifier's own cited evidence) actually satisfied it -- part of the fix converting ordered-milestone successCriteria from a reporting-only convention (docs/n8n-integration.md §9f) into an enforced runtime constraint: only the first not-yet-satisfied required milestone (in successCriteria declaration order) is ever eligible to be evaluated or satisfied, so a later required milestone can never be satisfied by evidence that only happens to overlap with an earlier page (e.g. a homepage's own persistent navigation advertising a destination it never actually reached). This same change also excludes persistent site-wide navigation/menu/header/footer chrome from semantic_page_match's own interactive-element vocabulary signal (src/core/semanticPageMatch.ts) -- a link living in that chrome is evidence a destination exists, never evidence it was reached. Neither the ordering enforcement nor the chrome exclusion required any new request-schema field: milestone order remains purely successCriteria's own declaration order, exactly as docs/n8n-integration.md §9f already documented. No existing field was removed, renamed, or had its meaning changed. Bumped from "1.8.0" to "1.9.0" earlier because status gained the additive "container_memory_threshold_reached" enum value and diagnostics.containerMemory (see $defs/containerMemoryDiagnostics) was added: the opt-in container-memory circuit breaker (MEMORY_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_ENABLED) reports its latest generic Linux cgroup memory sample and whether it stopped the run before the container's own OS-level OOM kill. Present only when that breaker was enabled for a run. Purely diagnostic, generic container-memory evidence -- never anything about the page/task/brand being run -- and additive: no existing field was removed, renamed, or had its meaning changed. Bumped from "1.7.0" to "1.8.0" earlier because diagnostics.resourceRouting (see $defs/resourceRoutingDiagnostics) was added: counts and approximate bytes of network requests allowed/blocked by the new opt-in LOW_MEMORY_BROWSER_MODE (see docs/architecture.md "Low-memory browser mode"), present only when that mode was enabled for a run. Purely diagnostic, generic Playwright resource-type evidence -- never anything about a specific site or brand -- and additive: no existing field was removed, renamed, or had its meaning changed. Bumped from "1.6.0" to "1.7.0" earlier because diagnostics.memory (see $defs/memorySample) was added: bounded process.memoryUsage() samples taken at run start, after each step, and after browser/context cleanup, so an out-of-memory incident can be correlated with the run's own memory trend rather than only inferred after the fact from platform-level restart events. Purely diagnostic, generic Node runtime evidence -- never anything about the page/task being run -- and additive: no existing field was removed, renamed, or had its meaning changed. Bumped from "1.5.0" to "1.6.0" earlier because observation.elementDiscoveryDiagnostics (see $defs/observation) was added: bounded, generic evidence about the interactive-element scan itself -- raw candidate count before filtering, button-like/link-like/other-role counts, per-reason excluded counts (zero-size, display:none, visibility:hidden), and a count of elements hosting an open shadow root -- so a caller can distinguish a genuinely empty page from one whose controls were excluded or live inside a structure the scan cannot see. No existing field was removed, renamed, or had its meaning changed. Bumped from "1.4.0" to "1.5.0" earlier because this repo's own versioning convention (see task-request.schema.json's schemaVersion description) bumps this const for every contract change, additive or not: this is the blocker-recovery response widening -- observation.interactiveElements[].frameOrigin and observation.inaccessibleFrameOrigins surface generic, one-level same-origin child-frame evidence; actionResult.staleTarget marks a failed action whose cause was mechanically classified as the target going stale (never a genuinely wrong decision); steps[].reObservationAttempted/recoveryAttempts surface the bounded pre-dispatch recovery cycle a step used; errors[].category gained the additive "stale_target_recovery" value; and the new opt-in host_context_snapshot capture module reports a bounded, names-only cookie/storage footprint on a cross-host transition. No existing field was removed, renamed, or had its meaning changed. Bumped from "1.3.0" to "1.4.0" earlier because observation.interactiveElements[].covered surfaces whether another element currently sits on top of a control's centre point, so the reasoning layer can see up front that a control is not actually clickable instead of only discovering it after a failed dispatch. Bumped from "1.2.0" to "1.3.0" earlier still because observation.interactiveElements[].disabled/ariaState and observation.progressIndicatorText widened the evidence surfaced to the reasoning/verification layers; captures.cta_clicks[].resultingTitle and captures.cta_clicks[].actionAnalytics (see $defs/actionAnalytics) added the generic, journey-agnostic action-attributed analytics record (dataLayer delta, GA4 window-correlated requests, resulting state, whether the action advanced the journey, and any semantic-verifier decisions attributable to it). Bumped from "1.1.0" to "1.2.0" earlier still for the additive diagnostics.domainDiscovery structure (see $defs/domainDiscoveryDiagnostics).

taskId.description: Echoes the taskId from the originating task-request.

statusReason.description: Short human-readable explanation of why the run ended in this status (e.g. which safety constraint triggered a block).

steps.description: Ordered log of every navigate/observe/decide/act cycle executed during the run.

target.description: Selector, element id, or URL the action applies to, when applicable.

params.description: Action-specific parameters (e.g. scroll distance, wait duration, navigate URL).

staleTarget.description: True only when a failed action's cause was mechanically classified as the target having gone stale (hidden, detached, covered/intercepted, timed out, or its owning frame becoming unavailable) between decision and dispatch -- never a genuinely wrong or unsafe decision. Drives the engine's bounded, non-fatal recovery for exactly this class of failure.

clickSideEffectDetected.description: True only when a bounded post-click check found generic evidence (a newly-appeared dialog/modal surface, or a materially different set of visible interactive controls) that this click produced a real interaction-state change -- including the case where the direct dispatch appeared to fail as intercepted/timed-out because the overlay it opened came to cover the trigger itself, so the click is reported as a success on that basis instead of falling through to the destinationUrl fallback. Absent (never false) whenever no such evidence was found or no check applied.

fallbackVerified.description: Present only when a generic destinationUrl navigation fallback was actually used to recover an unactionable click. True means the fallback's resulting page state was verified as a genuine, meaningful change (a different page path/origin, or generic evidence of a new interactive surface) rather than assumed equivalent to a real click; false means the fallback only changed the URL (e.g. a same-document hash-only navigation) with no verified further evidence.

openedNewContext.description: True only when this click produced a "popup" event (a target="_blank" anchor or a window.open() call from a click handler) -- regardless of whether that context was successfully instrumented. Absent (never false) whenever no such context was opened.

observedNewContext.description: Present only when openedNewContext is true. True when the opened context was actually adopted long enough to attach analytics capture to it before being closed; false when it closed, navigated away, or otherwise became unavailable before instrumentation could attach. Never asserts the context produced any particular evidence, only that it was observed at all.

estimatedCompletion.description: Engine's 0-1 estimate of progress toward success; a classification, not raw evidence.

observation.description: Compact structured summary of the page derived from visible and accessible elements. Never the raw HTML document.

interactiveElements.description: Condensed list of clickable/actionable elements available to the reasoning layer.

id.description: Stable reference the engine can resolve back to a Playwright locator.

destinationUrl.description: Destination URL of the element, when available (e.g. an anchor's href), surfaced to the reasoning layer so it can distinguish navigation targets without raw HTML.

disabled.description: True when the element carries a disabled attribute or aria-disabled="true".

ariaState.description: Generic ARIA selection/toggle-state attribute values present on this element (aria-selected/aria-checked/aria-pressed/aria-current), read verbatim from the page and never normalised into an engine-defined closed set.

covered.description: True when another element currently sits visually on top of this element's centre point (e.g. a modal, overlay, or banner), determined by the same elementFromPoint hit-test the engine uses to revalidate a click target immediately before dispatch. A covered element is still visible and still reported -- this only tells the reasoning layer it is not currently reachable by a click.

frameOrigin.description: Origin (scheme+host+port, never a full URL) of the same-origin child frame this element was found in -- present only for an element outside the main document. Absent for every main-document element, which remains the overwhelming common case.

nearestHeadingText.description: Short (<=80 char) text of the nearest enclosing heading (h1-h4), found via a bounded ancestor walk -- a cheap, markup-agnostic proxy for which repeated card/list-item this control is part of. Used to disambiguate route-memory candidate identity for controls that would otherwise share an identical role+accessibleName across multiple repeated cards. Absent when no heading was found within the bounded walk.

activeDialog.description: Present when a visible dialog/modal surface (role="dialog", aria-modal="true", or a native <dialog>) exists in the main document at the time of this observation. A compact, generic identity only -- never the dialog's full content, which is still carried element by element in interactiveElements as usual.

notableText.description: Short list of salient visible text snippets (headings, prices, banners) surfaced to the reasoning layer without sending full page content.

progressIndicatorText.description: Generic, brand-agnostic progress-indicator text (e.g. "Step 2 of 4"), read from any element the page itself marks up as a progress/step indicator (role="progressbar", aria-valuenow, aria-current="step").

inaccessibleFrameOrigins.description: Bounded (capped small), deduplicated list of origins of same-origin-scan-eligible child frames the engine detected but could not evaluate script in at the time of this observation (removed mid-scan, or otherwise inaccessible). Never frame content, never a reason beyond the fact that it couldn't be read.

elementDiscoveryDiagnostics.description: Bounded, generic diagnostic evidence about the interactive-element scan itself, always computed alongside interactiveElements -- lets a caller distinguish a genuinely empty page from one whose controls were excluded (hidden/zero-size) or live inside a structure this scan cannot see (a non-zero shadowHostCount alongside an empty interactiveElements is the generic signature of that specific gap). Summed across the main document and every accessible child frame, matching how interactiveElements itself is a flat cross-frame list.

rawElementCount.description: Every node matched by the same interactive-element selector interactiveElements is built from, before any visibility filtering. rawElementCount > 0 with interactiveElements empty means candidates existed but were all excluded; rawElementCount === 0 means the selector matched nothing at scan time at all.

buttonLikeCount.description: Of rawElementCount, elements whose role or tag is "button".

linkLikeCount.description: Of rawElementCount, elements whose role or tag is "a"/"link".

otherRoleCount.description: Of rawElementCount, everything else the selector matches (tabs, options, radio/checkbox-style controls, submit/button inputs, etc.). buttonLikeCount + linkLikeCount + otherRoleCount always equals rawElementCount.

visibleElementCount.description: Elements that survived the visibility filter -- equals interactiveElements.length for this same scan.

excludedZeroSizeCount.description: Of the excluded elements, how many had zero width or height. Not mutually exclusive with the other excluded*Count fields -- a single element can match more than one reason -- so these need not sum to (rawElementCount - visibleElementCount).

excludedDisplayNoneCount.description: Of the excluded elements, how many had computed style display: none.

excludedVisibilityHiddenCount.description: Of the excluded elements, how many had computed style visibility: hidden.

shadowHostCount.description: Count of elements in the document with a non-null, *open* shadow root. A closed shadow root's presence is fundamentally undetectable from outside the component that created it, so a page using closed shadow DOM can still report shadowHostCount: 0 despite hosting undiscoverable controls.

decision.description: Constrained rationale text produced by the reasoning layer for choosing the selected action.

progress.description: Snapshot of success-criteria evaluation after this step.

safetyFlags.description: Any guardrails that were evaluated and triggered on this step (e.g. domain_blocked, loop_detected, repeated_action, form_submission_blocked, required_criteria_unsatisfied).

reObservationAttempted.description: True when this step's pre-dispatch revalidation found the originally-decided click target no longer actionable and asked the reasoning provider again against a freshly rebuilt observation before dispatching anything.

recoveryAttempts.description: How many additional decision/revalidation cycles this step's pre-dispatch recovery used before settling on the action it actually dispatched -- bounded by a small fixed constant.

captures.description: Raw, website-derived evidence collected by capture modules, keyed by module name. Only modules the task requested are populated. This section must contain evidence as observed, not engine interpretation.

page_metadata.description: Generic per-page metadata (title, meta description, lang) as read from the document, with no engine interpretation.

finish_page_ctas.description: Visible calls-to-action found on the page at capture time (e.g. a journey's finish/success state). Generic element evidence only — no domain-specific classification.

text.description: Visible text of the CTA element as rendered on the page.

url.description: Destination URL of the CTA, when available (e.g. an anchor's href).

accessibleName.description: Accessible name (e.g. aria-label) of the CTA element, when available.

cta_clicks.description: CTAs the engine actually clicked, one entry per click action executed. Distinct from finish_page_ctas, which records all visible CTAs on a page regardless of whether they were clicked.

sourcePageUrl.description: URL of the page the CTA was clicked on.

ctaText.description: Visible text of the clicked CTA element as rendered on the page.

accessibleName.description: Accessible name (e.g. aria-label) of the clicked CTA element, when available.

destinationUrl.description: Destination URL of the CTA, when available (e.g. an anchor's href) at click time.

resultingUrl.description: Page URL after the click action completed, when known.

resultingTitle.description: Page title read immediately after the click action completed, when the click succeeded.

navigationSucceeded.description: Whether the click resulted in the page actually navigating to a new URL.

actionSucceeded.description: Whether the click action itself executed without error.

error.description: Error message when the click action did not succeed.

actionAnalytics.description: Generic, action-attributed analytics evidence for this click, present only when captureModules also requested data_layer_evidence and/or ga4_network_events.

journey_path.description: Complete ordered navigation history: one entry per completed navigate/observe/decide/act cycle. Generic across any task/domain.

pageUrlBefore.description: Page URL observed before the action was taken.

selectedElement.description: Details of the observed element the selected action targeted, when applicable.

decisionReason.description: Rationale supplied by the reasoning provider for choosing the selected action.

pageUrlAfter.description: Page URL after the action, falling back to pageUrlBefore when the action did not navigate.

raw.description: Unmodified dataLayer entries as read from the page at capture time.

source.description: Which browsing context/frame this entry was actually read from -- a generic, mechanical capture-provenance fact, never an interpretation of what the entry means.

frameOrigin.description: Origin (scheme+host+port) of the child frame this entry was read from -- present only for source: "child_frame".

contextId.description: Stable id distinguishing the tracked page ("main") from a specific adopted popup context.

truncated.description: True when this entry's raw array was cut down to the configured per-snapshot cap (oldest dropped first) -- never a silent truncation.

ref.description: Storage reference (path or URL) to the captured screenshot. The engine does not embed binary image data in this response.

reason.description: Why this screenshot was taken, e.g. "finish_state", "error", "scheduled".

errors.description: Raw technical diagnostics captured during the run: page JS errors, console errors, failed network requests, navigation/action failures, missing target elements, and safety/limit stops. Generic engine evidence, never converted into a business conclusion (see engineAssessment for that). Never contains cookies, auth headers, request bodies, credentials, tokens, personal data, or raw stack traces with environment paths.

stepIndex.description: Step during which this diagnostic was observed, when the engine has begun stepping. Absent for diagnostics observed before step 0 (e.g. during the initial navigation).

pageUrl.description: Page URL at the time this diagnostic was observed, when known.

actionType.description: Action type in effect when this diagnostic was observed, when applicable.

targetElementId.description: Engine-assigned element id (see observation.interactiveElements) the action targeted, when applicable. Never a raw selector or page content.

message.description: Concise, human-readable description of the diagnostic.

recoverable.description: Whether the run continued after this diagnostic was observed.

stoppedRun.description: Whether this diagnostic directly caused the run to stop.

displayedPrice.description: Price as displayed on the page, kept as text to preserve currency/formatting exactly as shown.

validityText.description: Visible validity/terms text as shown on the page, if any.

host_context_snapshot.description: Bounded, names-only footprint of cookies and localStorage/sessionStorage keys, captured only on the step this run's hostname changes (including the very first step, giving a landing-host baseline). Never a cookie or storage value -- see docs/architecture.md 'Blocker recovery'.

cookieNames.description: Cookie name/domain pairs from the whole browser context's cookie jar at this point -- never a value.

storageKeyNames.description: localStorage/sessionStorage key names present on the current page's own origin -- never a value.

engineAssessment.description: Engine-generated interpretation, kept separate from raw captures so downstream consumers never conflate observed evidence with classification.

summary.description: Short natural-language summary of what happened during the run.

notes.description: Any additional engine observations not captured elsewhere (e.g. anomalies noticed but not part of a capture module).

finishReason.description: Low-level reason the loop stopped, e.g. "stop_success_action", "max_steps", "domain_blocked", "unhandled_error".

engineVersion.description: Version of the navigation engine build that produced this response.

missingRequiredCriteriaIds.description: Ids of successCriteria entries with required !== false that were never satisfied by the time the run ended (e.g. a stop_success decision was rejected because required evidence was still missing, or the run stopped for another reason first). Present only when non-empty -- absent for a successful run, since the engine only honours stop_success once every required criterion is satisfied, and absent for any task with no required criteria at all.

memory.description: Bounded process.memoryUsage() samples taken at run start, after each step, and after browser/context cleanup -- generic Node runtime evidence only, never anything about the page/task being run. Exists to diagnose and correlate memory growth with incidents (e.g. an out-of-memory process kill) rather than to control engine behaviour. Present only when at least one sample was taken.

milestoneEvidence.description: One record per success criterion, appended the moment it first becomes satisfied (never re-recorded -- satisfiedCriteriaIds is a one-way ratchet, so a criterion contributes at most one record for the life of a run). Present only when at least one criterion was satisfied during the run.

milestoneEvidenceRecord.description: Explains why the engine judged one specific success criterion satisfied: which page it was evaluated against, in which phase of the step, and what evidence (a matched URL pattern, a matched selector, a deterministic vocabulary-overlap score, or a semanticVerifier's own cited evidence) actually satisfied it. This is engine classification (the "why"), kept in diagnostics rather than captures, which stays raw, website-derived evidence only.

criterionType.description: The criterion's own successCriteria[].type value, e.g. "semantic_page_match".

description.description: The criterion's own description text, echoed for readability.

phase.description: Whether this criterion was evaluated before this step's own action was dispatched, or immediately after it.

pageUrl.description: Page URL at the moment this criterion was judged satisfied.

evidenceSource.description: Which mechanism actually satisfied the criterion, e.g. "url_pattern", "element_present", "semantic_page_match:deterministic", "semantic_page_match:verifier", "data_layer_event", "network_event".

score.description: The deterministic vocabulary-overlap score, or semanticVerifier confidence, that satisfied this criterion, when applicable (semantic_page_match only).

matchedValue.description: The literal pattern/selector/match object that satisfied this criterion, when applicable.

reason.description: Short human-readable explanation of why the criterion was judged satisfied.

containerMemoryDiagnostics.description: The opt-in container-memory circuit breaker's (MEMORY_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_ENABLED) latest sample and outcome, from generic Linux cgroup memory accounting (cgroup v2, falling back to v1) -- see docs/architecture.md 'Container memory circuit breaker'. Present only when that breaker was enabled for this run. A single latest snapshot, not a growing history. available: false means this container did not expose readable cgroup memory files, so the breaker was inert for the whole run (never breaches) rather than failing the task.

version.description: Which cgroup version's memory files were read.

limitBytes.description: The container memory limit used (cgroup-reported, or MEMORY_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_LIMIT_BYTES if set).

latestSampleBytes.description: The most recent cgroup current-usage reading, in bytes.

breached.description: Whether the latest sample was at or above thresholdFraction of limitBytes, causing the run to stop early via the container_memory_threshold_reached status.

resourceRoutingDiagnostics.description: Counts and approximate bytes of network requests allowed/blocked by low-memory browser mode (LOW_MEMORY_BROWSER_MODE) -- see docs/architecture.md 'Low-memory browser mode'. Present only when that mode was enabled for this run.

byResourceType.description: One entry per Playwright request.resourceType() value actually seen during the run -- inherently bounded by Playwright's own small, fixed resource-type vocabulary, never per-request.

resourceRoutingEntry.description: One resource type's tally under low-memory browser mode. allowedBytesMeasured is summed from real Content-Length response headers (a measurement; requests without that header contribute 0, so this can under-count but never fabricates a number). blockedBytesEstimated is blockedCount times a fixed, documented per-resource-type average -- an estimate, never a measurement, since a blocked resource is never actually fetched.

resourceType.description: One of Playwright's own request.resourceType() values, e.g. "image", "script", "xhr" -- never anything about a specific site or brand.

memorySample.description: One process.memoryUsage() sample. See diagnostics.memory above.

reasoningProviderDecisionSummary.description: Safe per-decision usage summary for one reasoning-provider attempt. Never includes prompts, raw model responses, page content, request bodies, API keys, headers, or credentials.

stepIndex.description: Step index this decision was made for, when available (absent for a decision made before any step is known, e.g. an immediate fallback when no actions are allowed).

attempt.description: Attempt number within this decision: 0 is the first try, 1 is the single allowed retry, -1 marks a fallback produced without a model call.

confidence.description: Model-reported confidence for this decision, when available.

elementSelection.description: Bounded diagnostic of which interactive elements from this step's Observation actually reached the model's prompt for this attempt, and why.

consentControlIntent.description: This decision's self-reported consent semantics (see safety.consentInteractionPolicy's own description). Present whenever the provider produced a parseable response -- on acceptance and on a consent_policy_violation rejection alike -- so the full attempt-by-attempt consent history is auditable even when nothing was ultimately dispatched.

consentPolicyCompliant.description: Whether consentControlIntent (above) complied with this run's safety.consentInteractionPolicy, per the engine's deterministic enforcement. Present alongside consentControlIntent.

promptElementSelectionDiagnostic.description: Bounded diagnostic explaining which interactive elements from a step's Observation were actually included in one decision attempt's model prompt, and why (see src/reasoning/promptBuilder.ts). Never duplicates the full observation or the raw prompt -- `selected` is capped at the same per-step interactive-element limit already applied to the prompt itself, and `excludedRelevantCount` is a count only, never a list.

candidateCount.description: Total interactive elements observed on the page this step, before any truncation.

selectedCount.description: Number of elements actually included in the prompt sent to the model.

relevantSelectedCount.description: Of selectedCount, how many were selected because their accessible name shares literal vocabulary with the objective/successCriteria text.

structuralSelectedCount.description: Of selectedCount, how many were selected by the generic, language-independent structural/positional fallback (never text-based) rather than lexical relevance.

excludedRelevantCount.description: Count of elements that scored positively on lexical relevance but still did not fit within the prompt's element cap. A count only, never a list, to keep this diagnostic bounded.

selected.description: The elements actually included in the prompt, and why -- bounded to selectedCount entries.

reasoningProviderDiagnostics.description: Aggregated, per-run reasoning-provider usage diagnostics, derived from the provider's own decision log (never a second usage-tracking mechanism). Contains only safe aggregate/per-decision metadata -- never prompts, raw model responses, page content, request bodies, API keys, headers, or credentials. Reports token usage as source data for cost calculation downstream, not a computed monetary cost, since model pricing can change independently of this engine. Versioned independently of the top-level schemaVersion so this structure can evolve on its own.

version.description: Version of this reasoning-provider diagnostics structure, e.g. "1.2.0". Bumped from "1.1.0" to "1.2.0" for the consent-policy-enforcement audit trail (see safety.consentInteractionPolicy's own description): the additive, optional consentInteractionPolicy (the resolved policy for this run) and decisions[].consentControlIntent/consentPolicyCompliant -- no existing field removed or renamed. Bumped from "1.0.0" to "1.1.0" earlier for the additive, optional decisions[].elementSelection diagnostic -- no existing field removed or renamed.

provider.description: Reasoning provider that produced this run's decisions, e.g. "claude" or "mock".

model.description: Model identifier used by the provider, when applicable. Absent for the mock provider.

callCount.description: Number of real provider calls made this run, each counted once. Excludes immediate safe fallbacks produced without a call. Always 0 for the mock provider.

rejectedDecisionCount.description: Decisions rejected by engine-side validation or by a provider/API error.

fallbackDecisionCount.description: Decisions where the provider could not produce a valid decision and returned a safe stop_blocked fallback instead.

retryCount.description: Number of retry attempts (beyond each decision's first attempt) made this run.

consentInteractionPolicy.description: The resolved safety.consentInteractionPolicy (task-request.schema.json) this run actually enforced -- present so a caller can audit which policy applied even when the request itself omitted the field and the documented default ("reject_optional") applied instead. Absent only for a provider (e.g. the mock provider) that never resolved a policy.

decisions.description: Optional per-decision usage summary, one entry per attempt recorded in the provider's decision log.

semanticVerifierDecisionSummary.description: Safe per-decision usage summary for one SemanticCriterionVerifier attempt. Never includes prompts, raw model responses, page content, request bodies, API keys, headers, or credentials.

attempt.description: Attempt number within this verification call: 0 is the first try, 1 is the single allowed retry, -1 marks a reused cached verdict (cache_hit).

confidence.description: Model-reported confidence for this verification, when available.

evidence.description: Short evidence excerpt the model cited from the page signals already visible in Observation (title/headings/interactive element text), supporting or explaining its verdict.

semanticVerifierDiagnostics.description: Aggregated, per-run usage diagnostics for the optional SemanticCriterionVerifier -- a bounded, structured-output model call used only to adjudicate a semantic_page_match criterion the deterministic (lexical token-overlap) evaluator could not resolve (e.g. because the objective and the page are written in different languages), entirely separate from navigation decisions. See src/reasoning/semanticCriterionVerifier.ts and docs/n8n-integration.md 'Generic multilingual semantic_page_match verification'. Absent entirely when no verifier was configured for the run (the deterministic-only default). callCount excludes cacheHitCount: a cached verdict is reused for identical (criterion, page-evidence) pairs so an unchanged page is never re-verified across repeated stop_success attempts. Versioned independently of the top-level schemaVersion so this structure can evolve on its own.

provider.description: Provider that produced this run's semantic verifications, e.g. "claude".

callCount.description: Number of real model calls made this run (excludes cache hits).

cacheHitCount.description: Number of times a cached verdict was reused for unchanged (criterion, page-evidence) evidence instead of making a new model call.

rejectedCount.description: Verifications that did not satisfy the criterion, including malformed output, low confidence, missing evidence, or a provider/API error -- the verifier fails closed.

dataLayerDelta.description: Generic, mechanical before/after delta of window.dataLayer's contents around one click -- a cursor/position delta, never a full re-snapshot of either side. See src/capture-modules/dataLayerDelta.ts.

available.description: False when no dataLayer array existed on the page either before or after the click. True whenever a dataLayer array exists (even if newEntries is empty, meaning present but unchanged).

newEntries.description: Entries pushed to dataLayer since immediately before this click. When replaced is true, this is the entire post-click array (the prior contents no longer form a valid prefix, e.g. a full page navigation or an explicit reset).

replaced.description: True when the dataLayer array was reset or replaced rather than appended to.

actionAnalytics.description: Generic, action-attributed analytics evidence for one click the engine dispatched -- the single mechanism used for every journey, never a per-journey capture. GA4 field naming is deliberately non-causal: a request observed inside the bounded post-click window is temporally correlated with the click, never asserted to have been caused by it.

ga4RequestsObservedDuringActionWindow.description: GA4-style requests observed within a short, fixed window after this click. Correlation, not causation.

advancedJourney.description: True iff the URL or title changed, or a success criterion newly became satisfied, as a direct result of this click.

newlySatisfiedCriteriaIds.description: Ids of success criteria that were unsatisfied before this click and satisfied immediately after it.

verifierDecisions.description: Any semanticVerifier decisions made while evaluating success criteria immediately after this click.

trustedDomainEntry.description: One hostname the run trusted for navigation, and why.

sourceUrl.description: The URL this trust decision was derived from, when applicable (absent for caller_supplied).

externalDomainCandidate.description: A hostname discovered during preflight on a different registrable domain than the site being navigated. Never auto-trusted -- surfaced here so a caller/operator can review and explicitly add it to the task's allowedDomains if the run is meant to cross into it.

reason.description: Human-readable explanation of why this candidate was not auto-trusted.

rejectedDomainCandidate.description: A URL considered during preflight and rejected outright by the conservative candidate-validation policy (unsupported protocol, localhost, loopback, or link-local address).

domainDiscoveryDiagnostics.description: Diagnostics from the engine's deterministic preflight domain-discovery phase, which runs before the Claude-driven navigation loop and proposes an allowedDomains set so a caller need not enumerate every domain/subdomain a journey might use. See docs/architecture.md 'Preflight domain discovery' for the full conservative validation policy this reflects.

startRegistrableDomain.description: Registrable (eTLD+1) domain of the start hostname, resolved via a maintained Public Suffix List-backed library. Null for hosts with no PSL-registrable domain (bare IPs, "localhost", or a hostname that is itself only a public suffix).

finalUrl.description: URL the initial navigation actually landed on, after following any HTTP redirects from startUrl.

redirectChain.description: Ordered list of URLs visited following a redirect from startUrl through to finalUrl (inclusive of both ends).

canonicalUrl.description: The landed page's <link rel="canonical"> URL, when present.

trustedDomains.description: Every hostname trusted for this run, and why -- the union of caller-supplied allowedDomains and everything preflight discovery proposed.

externalCandidates.description: Hostnames discovered on a different registrable domain than the site being navigated, never auto-trusted.

rejectedCandidates.description: URLs rejected outright during preflight discovery by the conservative candidate-validation policy.

proposedAllowedDomains.description: Hostnames preflight discovery itself proposed (excludes hostnames the caller already supplied explicitly).

allowedDomainsUsed.description: The final allowedDomains set actually enforced for this run: caller-supplied allowedDomains (if any) unioned with proposedAllowedDomains.

blockedReason.description: Present only when preflight discovery itself blocked the run (e.g. the initial navigation redirected to an unsafe host).

params.description: Raw query/body parameters observed on the outgoing GA4 network request.

method.description: HTTP method of the outgoing request, e.g. "GET", "POST".

postDataRaw.description: Raw POST/sendBeacon request body, bounded and truncated (never dropped) past a fixed size cap. Absent for a GET request, or a POST/sendBeacon request with no body.

postDataParams.description: Body parameters, generically parsed only when the raw body is unambiguously form-urlencoded -- never a client-specific parsing rule. One entry per newline-delimited hit (a batched GA4 sendBeacon body concatenates multiple hits this way). Absent when the body doesn't confidently parse this way.

measurementId.description: Mechanically read from the standard GA4 Measurement Protocol "tid" parameter (query or body) when present. Never inferred when absent.

consentState.description: Mechanically read from the standard GA4 consent-state parameters ("gcs", "dma", "dma_cps") when present, verbatim. Never inferred when absent.

source.description: Which browsing context/frame this request was actually observed on -- a generic, mechanical capture-provenance fact, never an interpretation of what the request means.

contextId.description: Stable id distinguishing the tracked page ("main") from a specific adopted popup context.

frameOrigin.description: Origin of the child frame this request originated from -- present only for source: "child_frame".

truncated.description: True when postDataRaw was cut down to the configured size cap -- never a silent truncation.
